title: Why Does a Language Model Need Post-Training?

images.caption: The same request, two models. The base model's likeliest next word starts another assignment; after post-training it starts an answer. Probabilities and replies are illustrative, modeled on OpenAI's published GPT-3 vs InstructGPT example, not measured.
images.target_after_text: This article explains why we need it, how it differs from pretraining, and the three techniques it usually involves.
images.target_after_text_full: This article explains why we need it, how it differs from pretraining, and the three techniques it usually involves.
images.target_block_html: This article explains why we need it, how it differs from pretraining, and the three techniques it usually involves.

images.caption: One model, two stages. Pretraining pours in a huge stream of raw text; post-training feeds the same model three small, curated streams: examples, comparisons and checked answers. Volumes are not to scale.
images.target_after_text: Post-training doesn't build a new model. It keeps training the same one. What changes is the data and the signal that t...
images.target_after_text_full: Post-training doesn't build a new model. It keeps training the same one. What changes is the data and the signal that tells the model what "better" means.
images.next_text: Goal. Pretraining: predict the next word in text. Post-training: behave the way people want, which means following inst...
images.next_text_full: Goal. Pretraining: predict the next word in text. Post-training: behave the way people want, which means following instructions, staying safe, and getting answers right.
images.target_block_html: Post-training doesn't build a new model. It keeps training the same one. What changes is the data and the signal that tells the model what "better" means.

images.caption: Pretraining and post-training side by side: goal, data, signal, cost and how much the model changes.
images.target_after_text: Roughly: pretraining gives the model what it knows; post-training shapes how it uses it.
images.target_after_text_full: Roughly: pretraining gives the model what it knows; post-training shapes how it uses it.
images.next_text: Small data can still change behavior a lot. In one study, mixing just 500 safety examples into a large instruction data...
images.next_text_full: Small data can still change behavior a lot. In one study, mixing just 500 safety examples into a large instruction dataset was enough to substantially reduce harmful responses.
images.target_block_html: Roughly: pretraining gives the model what it knows; post-training shapes how it uses it.

images.caption: Instruction tuning. The instruction is context only; the model is graded on each word of the response. Words are revealed one at a time for readability; training grades them all in one pass.
images.target_after_text: This is also called supervised fine-tuning (SFT), because every instruction comes with a correct answer to imitate. Tra...
images.target_after_text_full: This is also called supervised fine-tuning (SFT), because every instruction comes with a correct answer to imitate. Trained across many kinds of tasks, the model gets better at following instructions in general, including tasks it never saw.
images.target_block_html: This is also called supervised fine-tuning (SFT), because every instruction comes with a correct answer to imitate. Trained across many kinds of tasks, the model gets better at following instructions in general, including tasks it never saw.

images.caption: Preference alignment. The preferred answer becomes more likely and the other less likely, while a leash keeps the model near the original. Simplified: the judge route (RLHF) and DPO share one picture.
images.target_after_text: Without the leash, the model could chase high scores, drift far from its starting point, and forget much of what it lea...
images.target_after_text_full: Without the leash, the model could chase high scores, drift far from its starting point, and forget much of what it learned in pretraining.
images.target_block_html: Without the leash, the model could chase high scores, drift far from its starting point, and forget much of what it learned in pretraining.

images.caption: RLVR. The model tries several answers; a checker marks each right or wrong, and the right answer becomes more likely round by round. This checker reads only the final answer.
images.target_after_text: That makes RLVR well suited to the long, multi-step problems where base models struggle. One caution: a checker is only...
images.target_after_text_full: That makes RLVR well suited to the long, multi-step problems where base models struggle. One caution: a checker is only as good as its rule. If it checks only the final answer, it says nothing about whether every step was sound.
images.target_block_html: That makes RLVR well suited to the long, multi-step problems where base models struggle. One caution: a checker is only as good as its rule. If it checks only the final answer, it says nothing about whether every step was sound.
